parts.part: A month always in view, not in a picker

leaves.what: RangeCalendar, CalendarGrid, CalendarGridHeader, CalendarHeaderCell, CalendarGridBody, CalendarCell and Heading from react-aria-components, in src/schedule/MonthRange.tsx
leaves.why: The kit exports no calendar that stands on the page: its calendar exists only inside DatePicker and DateRangePicker (DockedCalendar, ModalCalendar, RangeMonth are private to DatePicker.tsx).

leaves.what: Read DatePicker.tsx past its doc comment (RangeMonth, DockedHeader) and date-picker-styles.ts to learn the cell's DOM (cell > band + day > state layer + text), the group/dpi contract, slot="previous"/"next" on IconButton and slot={null} on a button that is neither
leaves.why: The style module is documented as what the pickers draw from, but nothing says how to draw a calendar of one's own with it; the nesting the band and the range ends depend on is only in the picker's source.
It is not in the barrel (index.ts), though it is the only way to get Material's calendar look outside a picker.

leaves.what: The calendar's header (month heading, Today, previous, next), a dot under a day that has appointments, the card around it and the hint under it

parts.notes: Not seen in a browser (none allowed): checked by the build and one server render (35 grid cells, a selected cell). The dot is aria-hidden: a screen reader is not told which days hold appointments. The grid is 336px wide; it fits a 360px window with the page's 12px gutters, no narrower. Weeks start on the locale's first day. The weekday row is the style module's (body-large, on-surface) with short names ('Mon') where the kit's pickers draw one letter.

leaves.what: The same RangeCalendar: its value is the range, controlled by the page; the range drives the list (one section a day), the heading above it, the count, and the date a new appointment opens on
leaves.why: The kit's DateRangePicker is always a full-screen dialog behind a field; there is no range calendar to place on a page.

parts.notes: A single day takes two presses on the same day (React Aria's range selection); the range defaults to today, 'Today' puts it back, and a line under the month says so. By keyboard: arrows, Enter to start, Enter to end, Page Up/Down for months. Saving an appointment outside the range moves the range to its day.

leaves.what: TimeField, DateInput, DateSegment, Label, FieldError and Text from react-aria-components, as src/components/TimeField.tsx: a start and an end typed in place in the event's dialog
leaves.why: The kit has TimePicker only: a button-shaped trigger that opens a modal dial. Nothing is typed in place, and inside the event's dialog it would stack a second modal for each of the two times.
TimePicker has no isInvalid, errorMessage, isRequired or name: 'the end is before the start' and 'the practitioner is busy then' have nowhere to show on it.

leaves.what: Read field-styles.ts (the segmented kind, its slots and compound variants) and DatePicker.tsx's SegmentedField and Supporting to mirror them
leaves.why: field-styles says a segmented field holds 'hour, minute' segments, but no kit component is a time field and the slots' wiring (base on the root, container, input, label after it, state layer, indicator, supporting) is only in the pickers' source.

parts.notes: Changing the start moves the end by the same length; choosing a visit sets the end to its usual length. Errors show after the first submit. A press on the field's empty part (right of the segments) may not put the focus in the first segment: not checked in a browser. The trailing clock is decorative, not a button. Hour cycle is the locale's.

leaves.what: Used Modal + Dialog in place of ModalDialog
leaves.why: ModalDialog passes no class to the modal, and DialogContent is w-full in a modal that has no width: the dialog would be as wide as its content. Modal's className (on the inner modal) gave it 'w-full max-w-140 px-4', which fits 400px and stops at 560px.

leaves.what: Passed 'max-h-dvh overflow-auto' to the dialog so a form taller than the window scrolls
leaves.why: DialogContent is overflow-hidden with no maximum height, and with children it has no scrolling body or pinned actions.
The outlined fields' label notch defaults to 'surface'; field-styles.ts documents this arbitrary property as the way to match a dialog's ground. The kit's Dialog does not set it itself.

leaves.what: Read DialogContent's and Modal's bodies to learn that children replace the headline and the actions, and which element className lands on
leaves.why: Dialog's comment says children replace everything; where a width or a height goes is not said.

leaves.what: The form: headline, fields in one and two columns, the action row (Cancel appointment at the start, Close and Save at the end), validation in the component's state
leaves.why: Composition; with children, the dialog's actions are the caller's.

leaves.what: Read Select.tsx's body and React Stately's select types to learn how the chosen option is passed (selectedKey / onSelectionChange, spread onto React Aria's Select) and what SelectItem takes (label, supportingText)
leaves.why: Select's doc comment shows items and children only, no controlled value.

parts.notes: One dialog adds (the app bar's and the empty state's button) and opens an existing appointment (a row of the list) to change or cancel it; cancelling shows a snackbar with Undo. Validation: patient, date, times, end after start, and a clash with the same practitioner's other appointments. react-hook-form's adapter was not used: plain state was enough. Not seen in a browser: the docked DatePicker's popover over the modal, the scroll at 400px and the notch colour are unverified. Select uses selectedKey/onSelectionChange, which type-check. A server render of the form (new and existing) shows both selects' chosen options, the date's and the times' segments and the cancel button only on an existing appointment.

parts.part: A list of the day's events

leaves.what: GridListSection and GridListHeader from react-aria-components: one section a day when the range holds several
leaves.why: The kit's GridList has no section or header of its own.

leaves.what: useLocale from react-aria-components, with DateFormatter from @internationalized/date, for the times and the days' names
leaves.why: The kit formats nothing for the caller; the guidance lists useLocale as React Aria's to use.

leaves.what: The row's leading time column (start over end, font-mono, label-large), the section header, the heading with the range and the count above the list, the centred loader
Read Tag.tsx's variants for its colour names, and Typography.tsx for colorRole and component
leaves.why: Tag's comment shows two colours by example and no list; the type primitives' props are in the source's variant table.

parts.notes: A row opens its appointment by press, Enter or Space; arrows move through rows across days. Each new range 'loads' for 600ms behind a LoadingIndicator; the count line is a polite live region. Days of a range with nothing booked are not listed; a range with nothing at all shows the EmptyState with an add button. The Tag stays beside a long name at 400px and the text wraps: not seen in a browser. The day's header text is a span in React Aria's header row, not a heading element.

general_leaves.what: The page: TopAppBar with the add button in its actions, then the month card and the list in a column, side by side from lg
general_leaves.why: Composition. No block served a part: a pager, a stepper, radio tiles, a reading carousel and a site header are none of this screen's five.

general_leaves.what: Read icons.tsx for an icon's props, TopAppBar's props type, and Snackbar's option types
general_leaves.why: Small lookups past the doc comments: what a kit icon accepts when drawn directly, and the shape of snackbar's action.

general_leaves.what: Unseen at 400px: the top app bar holds the title, a subtitle and a labelled 'New appointment' button on one row
general_leaves.why: No browser was allowed; if it crowds, the button should become an icon button or a FAB on a phone.

friction: The build was green at the first run and nothing was guessed wrong, but only after reading about 400 lines of DatePicker.tsx and field-styles.ts. (1) The kit has Material's whole calendar, in single and range form, and exports none of it: a Calendar and a RangeCalendar component (or the style module in the barrel with a ten-line example of the cell's DOM) would have made parts 1 and 2 kit parts. (2) There is no TimeField: the segmented field kind is ready for one and its comment names hour and minute, but the only time control is a modal dial with no validation props. A kit TimeField (and isInvalid/errorMessage on TimePicker) would have covered part 3. (3) ModalDialog gives no way to size the dialog or let a long form scroll, and the dialog does not set --md3-field-notch for outlined fields inside it; a 'form in a dialog' example in Dialog's comment (width, scroll, notch, actions with children) would have saved the reading. (4) GridList's comment does not say whether sections exist; a line pointing at React Aria's GridListSection in the 'straight from React Aria' table would do. (5) ds-build's table of what to read is good; a line 'no inline calendar, no typed time field: build on RangeCalendar/TimeField with date-picker-styles and field-styles' under 'Use what exists' would have turned the search into a lookup. Nothing could be looked at: every visual claim rests on the build, the lint and one server render.
